previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Initially concerning for C. difficile given recent antibiotic use, stool studies were negative. Urine culture grew E. coli, confirming a complicated urinary tract infection. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone, then transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. Renal transplant ultrasound was normal, and creatinine remained at baseline. She improved clinically, with resolution of fever and abdominal symptoms. She was discharged home on a full course of antibiotics with instructions to follow up with her primary and nephrology teams.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Other and unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli]

ACUTE ISSUES
# Klebsiella UTI: Patient presented with fever nausea and 
vomiting. She had a notable history of UTIs with resultant 
bacteremia. Previous UTIs grew pan sensitive E. Coli. Given her 
history of renal transplant she was pan-cultured, CXR and 
renal/abdominal ultrasound. Studies revealed UTI without 
evidence of renal involvement. Given history of bacteremia and 
systemic symptoms she was started on IV ceftriaxone for a 
duration of 4 days. She had a recurrent fever over the IV 
antibiotics the first night so she was broadened to Cefepime for 
24 hours until Urine culture returned with Klebsiella sensitive 
to ceftriaxone so she was switched back. She was discharged with 
ciprofloxacin 500 BID for 14 days total, last dose on ___. 
Of note her adverse reaction of c-diff infection to PO cipro was 
noted however unfortunately she was diagnosed with c-diff (see 
below)  on this admission therefore in order to avoid IV 
antibiotics as an outpatient she ws put on treatment for both. 
Additional details below.

# Diarrhea: Patient developed diarrhea on her ___ hospital day 
and stool was cultured for C-diff, extended culture was sent and 
CMV viral load was also sent. CMV viral load was negative but 
c-diff was positive. Remainder of stool studeis pending on 
discharge. She was started on metronidazole 500 Q8H for an 
extended course given that she was put on ciprofloxacin to avoid 
IV antibiotcs. Her course is to be continued two weeks after 
last dose of ciprofloxacin. Last dose of metronidazole on 
___. 

# ___: patient presented with acute on chronic kidney injury as 
a results of poor PO intake. It was corrected with IV fluids and 
Cr was 1.5 on discharge.
 
# ESRD s/p LURT ___ - Patient with history of renal transplant 
secondary to FSGN with recent Cr values of 1.3. Sirolimus 1mg 
daily and Tacrolimus 1mg BID were continued with Tacro levels 
ranging from 5.7-7.4. Calcitriol 0.5 mcg  also continued and 
nephrology followed closely. OTc was monitored and was normal 
throughout admission.

# CAD s/p NSTEMI / Hypertension / Hyperlipidemia
